## Topics

### Geocentric to Heliocentric Paradigm Shift
The 2,000-year journey from Aristotle's geocentric model through Aristarchus, Ptolemy, Copernicus, Kepler, Galileo, Newton, and Einstein, illustrating how long paradigm shifts can take and drawing parallels to the future acceptance of Bowen Theory.
*_(~18% of transcript; Sections 8-21)_*

### Forces in Physical and Biological Worlds
Frank Wilczek's description of the elementary particles and physical laws of the universe, and the question of what physical forces and properties carry over into biological systems and ultimately into human emotional functioning.
*_(~10% of transcript; Sections 22-29)_*

### Cancer as Blocked Ontogeny and Cell Differentiation
Researchers Sonenschein, Soto, and Bertoloso's work framing cancer as a disease of blocked cell differentiation rather than multiplication, with regressing cells reverting to ancestral properties, and the parallels drawn to Bowen Theory's concept of blocked development through undifferentiation.
*_(~18% of transcript; Sections 30-43)_*

### Core Affect, Homeostasis, and the Emotional Brain
Leonard Mlodinow's concept of core affect as a neurological sentinel monitoring threats to homeostasis, and how emotions evolved as a flexible response system in organisms, connecting to Bowen's view of the intellectual and emotional systems as a working team.
*_(~8% of transcript; Sections 55-58)_*

### Wanting versus Liking: Reward System Neuroscience
Kent Berridge's research distinguishing the brain's separate subsystems for pleasure (liking) and motivation (wanting), including dopamine's role in wanting circuits and the implications for understanding driven behavior in human emotional functioning.
*_(~10% of transcript; Sections 59-63)_*

### Salience Network, Executive Control Network, and Determination
William Seeley's identification of the emotional salience network and executive control network in the brain, and the serendipitous discovery of a neural node for determination, connecting brain-level findings to the capacity for self-regulation described in Bowen Theory.
*_(~12% of transcript; Sections 65-72)_*

### Chronic Anxiety as Vigilance and Homeostatic Disturbance
Discussion among participants and Dr. Kerr on chronic anxiety as an internalized vigilance pattern shaped by family emotional programming, its relationship to homeostatic disturbance, and whether it functions as a driver of regression or a motivator for change.
*_(~12% of transcript; Sections 45, 73-87)_*
